proofs.proof_tex:
Assume \(U=\varnothing\), put \(n=|V|\), and put \(m=\max_{i\in V}|\Omega_i|\).  The input conditions that \(V\) and all \(\Omega_i\) are finite and nonempty imply \(n\geq 1\) and \(m\geq 1\).  Identification means that, for any \(M_1,M_2\in\mathfrak M(G,\Omega,W,\Pi)\),
\[
 P_{M_1}(V)=P_{M_2}(V)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad q(M_1)=q(M_2).
 \tag{1}
\]
Thus the causal target \(q(M)=P_{M,x}(Y=y)\) is not being defined as an observed-law functional; equality with such a functional will be derived below.

Fix an exact support \(S\) realized by a member of \(\mathfrak M(G,\Omega,W,\Pi)\).  For a vertex \(i\in V\) and an assignment \(a\) to its parents in \(G\), define
\[
 A_i^S(a)=\{b\in\Omega_i:\text{there is }v\in S
       \text{ such that }v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)}=a
       \text{ and }v_i=b\}.
 \tag{2}
\]
Call the row \(o=(i,a)\) reached when \(A_i^S(a)\neq\varnothing\).  If \(M\) has exact support \(S\), then at every reached row
\[
 P_M(i=b\mid\operatorname{pa}_G(i)=a)
 =\frac{P_M(i=b,\operatorname{pa}_G(i)=a)}
        {P_M(\operatorname{pa}_G(i)=a)}.
 \tag{3}
\]
The denominator is positive because (2) supplies a state in \(S\) with parent assignment \(a\).  Hence the observed law uniquely determines every reached conditional row, and the positive entries in that row are exactly those indexed by \(A_i^S(a)\).  If \(i\in W\), the functional-node assumption makes every row a point mass, so a reached row satisfies \(|A_i^S(a)|=1\).  An unreached row has zero observational probability of being invoked.

We next prove the support-preservation fact used below.  Define
\[
 J(S)=\left\{v:\text{for every }i\in V,\ 
 A_i^S(v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})=\varnothing
 \text{ or }v_i\in A_i^S(v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})\right\}.
 \tag{4}
\]
For every fully observed Bayesian-network law with exact support \(S\),
\[
 S=J(S).
 \tag{5}
\]
The inclusion \(S\subseteq J(S)\) follows immediately from (2).  For the reverse inclusion, order the vertices topologically as \(i_1,\ldots,i_n\) and fix \(v\in J(S)\).  Suppose inductively that the conditional factors for the first \(k-1\) coordinates of \(v\) are positive.  The initial topological segment is ancestral, so summing the DAG factorization over later variables, using normalization of their conditional rows in reverse topological order, shows that the probability of the first \(k-1\) coordinates is the product of those positive factors.  It is therefore positive, and some state of \(S\) extends that prefix.  All parents of \(i_k\) occur in the prefix, so the row \((i_k,v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i_k)})\) is reached.  Membership in \(J(S)\) then gives \(v_{i_k}\in A_{i_k}^S(v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i_k)})\), and (3) makes the corresponding conditional factor positive.  The induction starts with the empty prefix.  At \(k=n\), the DAG factorization gives \(P_M(V=v)>0\), so \(v\in S\), proving (5).

Consequently, two collections of conditional tables having the same reached rows, with positive support \(A_i^S(a)\) on each such row, and arbitrary normalized fills on unreached rows induce the same observed law and retain exact support \(S\).  Indeed, a state in \(S\) uses only common reached-row entries.  If \(v\notin S=J(S)\), (4) fails at some reached row and \(v_i\notin A_i^S(v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})\), so both factorizations assign probability zero to \(v\).  This argument uses neither global positivity nor positivity of an unreached row.  The finite enumeration asserted by \(\mathrm{lem:support-oracle}\) decides which supports are realizable and which rows are reached.

Suppose now that the realized support \(S\) admits a completion obstruction.  By \(\mathrm{def:completion-obstruction}\), there are two deterministic complete tables \(t_1,t_2\) which agree at every reached row, obey the point-mass restrictions at \(W\), and satisfy
\[
 e_j:=\mathbf 1\{Y_x(t_j)=y\},\qquad |e_1-e_2|=1.
 \tag{6}
\]
Write \(b_o\in A_i^S(a)\) for their common output at the reached row \(o=(i,a)\).  Fix any integer \(r\geq 3\), and set
\[
 \varepsilon_r=\frac{1}{rn}.
 \tag{7}
\]
At every reached row \(o=(i,a)\), with \(k_o=|A_i^S(a)|\), use in both models the row
\[
 \theta_{o,r}(b)
 =(1-\varepsilon_r)\mathbf 1\{b=b_o\}
 +\frac{\varepsilon_r}{k_o}\mathbf 1\{b\in A_i^S(a)\}.
 \tag{8}
\]
At each unreached row, model \(M_j^{(r)}\) retains the corresponding deterministic row of \(t_j\).  Equation (8) is normalized and has positive support exactly \(A_i^S(a)\).  For a reached row of a vertex in \(W\), one has \(k_o=1\), so (8) is a point mass; the unreached rows of such a vertex are point masses by the definition of the completion.  Thus both models satisfy the functional-node assumption.  Because \(U=\varnothing\), the independent-root condition is vacuous.  The support-preservation result following (5) shows that the two models have the same observed law and exact support \(S\).  For every event literal appearing in \(\Pi\), positivity is equivalent to the corresponding cylinder meeting \(S\), and probability zero is equivalent to that cylinder being disjoint from \(S\).  Since \(S\) was realized by a model satisfying \(\Pi\), both \(M_1^{(r)}\) and \(M_2^{(r)}\) satisfy all support literals.  Hence
\[
 M_1^{(r)},M_2^{(r)}\in\mathfrak M(G,\Omega,W,\Pi),
 \qquad P_{M_1^{(r)}}(V)=P_{M_2^{(r)}}(V),
 \qquad \operatorname{supp}_V(M_j^{(r)})=S.
 \tag{9}
\]

Couple an interventional execution of \(M_j^{(r)}\) with the deterministic execution of \(t_j\).  At an encountered reached row, generate (8) by retaining \(b_o\) with probability \(1-\varepsilon_r\) and otherwise drawing uniformly from \(A_i^S(a)\).  Conditional on every preceding value, the probability that this output differs from the baseline is
\[
 \varepsilon_r\left(1-\frac1{k_o}\right)\leq\varepsilon_r.
 \tag{10}
\]
At an encountered unreached row it is zero.  At most \(n\) vertices are evaluated.  Repeated subadditivity of probability, applied to the deviation event at each adaptively encountered row, therefore gives
\[
 \Pr(\text{some evaluated output differs from the baseline})
 \leq n\varepsilon_r=\frac1r.
 \tag{11}
\]
If no deviation occurs, the interventional outcome agrees with the deterministic execution.  Thus, for \(j\in\{1,2\}\),
\[
 \left|q(M_j^{(r)})-e_j\right|\leq\frac1r.
 \tag{12}
\]
Combining (6) and (12) with the triangle inequality yields the parameterized separation
\[
 \left|q(M_1^{(r)})-q(M_2^{(r)})\right|
 \geq 1-\frac2r>0.
 \tag{13}
\]

The arithmetic bounds also follow directly from (8).  At a reached row with \(k=k_o\), a nonselected allowed value has probability
\[
 \frac1{rnk},
\]
whereas the selected value has probability
\[
 1-\frac1{rn}+\frac1{rnk}=\frac{rnk-k+1}{rnk}.
 \tag{14}
\]
All other primitive entries are zero or one.  After reducing each fraction separately, every denominator is at most
\[
 rnk\leq rnm=:D_r.
 \tag{15}
\]
The numerator and denominator of each reduced primitive fraction are at most \(D_r\); with the usual binary representation, their combined length is therefore at most
\[
 2\left\lceil\log_2 D_r\right\rceil+2
 =2\left\lceil\log_2\!\left(r|V|\max_{i\in V}|\Omega_i|\right)\right\rceil+2.
 \tag{16}
\]
No common denominator is used, and every induced observational or interventional cell is an exact finite sum of products of these primitive fractions.

The quantifiers in (7)--(16) are important.  For each obstruction and each chosen integer \(r\geq3\), (8) existentially selects an observational fiber on which the two models have the separation (13).  The claim is not that every fixed observational law having exact support \(S\) admits a same-law pair with this constant gap.  Taking \(r=8\) gives the stated \(3/4\)-gap construction and the denominator bound \(8nm\).  Letting \(r\) grow makes the certified gaps approach one, while (16) increases by only \(O(\log r)\) primitive bits for the fixed input.  In particular, an obstruction contradicts identification as defined in (1).

Conversely, suppose that no exact support realized in the model class admits a completion obstruction.  Fix \(M\in\mathfrak M(G,\Omega,W,\Pi)\), write \(P=P_M(V)\), and let \(S=\operatorname{supp}_V(M)\).  Independently for every conditional-table row of \(M\), draw one output according to that row's probability vector.  This produces a random deterministic complete table \(T\).  Rows belonging to \(W\) remain deterministic by the functional-node assumption.  In one acyclic execution under \(\operatorname{do}(X=x)\), each nonintervened vertex invokes exactly one row.  Independence of the row draws and finite expansion over assignments therefore give
\[
 \Pr(Y_x(T)=y)
 =\sum_{v:\,v_X=x,\ v_Y=y}
       \prod_{i\notin X}P_M(v_i\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)})
 =P_{M,x}(Y=y)=q(M),
 \tag{17}
\]
where the second equality is the truncated DAG factorization obtained by replacing the mechanisms at \(X\) by the point mass at \(x\).

Condition on all deterministic outputs drawn at reached rows.  Each such output belongs to the corresponding set \(A_i^S(a)\).  If the indicator \(\mathbf 1\{Y_x(T)=y\}\) differed for two choices of the unreached rows under this fixed reached-row realization, those two deterministic tables would be a completion obstruction.  By hypothesis no such pair exists.  Hence, for each fixed realization of the reached rows, the indicator is constant over all deterministic fills of the unreached rows.  Its conditional expectation is therefore independent of the unreached stochastic rows.  If \(M'\in\mathfrak M(G,\Omega,W,\Pi)\) has observed law \(P\), then it has the same exact support \(S\), and (3) shows that all of its reached rows equal those of \(M\).  The distribution of the reached-row draws is consequently the same, so averaging the same conditional constants in (17) gives
\[
 q(M')=q(M).
 \tag{18}
\]
This proves identification when no realized support has an obstruction.

It remains to construct the identifying map explicitly.  For each realizable support \(S\), choose once and for all a value \(h_S^0(i,a)\in\Omega_i\) at every unreached row, using the resulting point mass at every such row of a vertex in \(W\).  On the branch \(\operatorname{supp}(P)=S\), define
\[
 \kappa_{i,S}(b\mid a;P)=
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle\frac{P(i=b,\operatorname{pa}_G(i)=a)}
 {P(\operatorname{pa}_G(i)=a)},&A_i^S(a)\neq\varnothing,\\[1.2ex]
 \mathbf 1\{b=h_S^0(i,a)\},&A_i^S(a)=\varnothing,
 \end{cases}
 \tag{19}
\]
and
\[
 F_S(P)=\sum_{v:\,v_X=x,\ v_Y=y}
             \prod_{i\notin X}\kappa_{i,S}
             (v_i\mid v_{\operatorname{pa}_G(i)};P).
 \tag{20}
\]
Every denominator in the first branch of (19) is positive by the support guard and (2)--(3); the second branch uses no division.  Put \(F_S=0\) on an unrealizable support branch.  Because the observed product alphabet is finite, there are finitely many such branches, and (19)--(20) form a support-valid guarded formula in the sense of \(\mathrm{def:guarded-formula}\).

For a model \(M\) with support \(S\), the reached rows in (19) are its actual rows by (3).  Equation (17), followed by the proved invariance with respect to all unreached-row fills, then gives
\[
 q(M)=F_{\operatorname{supp}_V(M)}(P_M(V)).
 \tag{21}
\]
Thus the observed-law functional (20) has been derived from the causal truncated factorization.  Equations (9)--(16) prove the separating direction, including its parameterized existential-fiber and rational-encoding guarantees; equations (17)--(21) prove the guarded-formula direction.  Together they establish the claimed equivalence and, at \(r=8\), every numerical assertion in the stated theorem.

proposed.comparator_claim: The ID algorithm is sound and complete for ordinary latent causal effect identification.

Theorem 15 gives functional-variable elimination under its stated separability and parent conditions; Theorem 18 assumes the treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\).
Arithmetic-circuit invariant-cut tests address constrained identifiability, including logical and \(0\)--\(1\) constraints.

Theorems 1--2 prove soundness of formula-returning algorithms for state-based causal effects under context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints; the paper assumes a strictly positive observational distribution and does not claim completeness under those constraints.
A formula may require positivity only for the events introduced in its derivation.
Theorem 5 makes Algorithm 1 terminating and sound, while Theorem 6 shows that identification in every context-specific DAG need not imply identification from the observed law.
Completeness holds for context-specific independences controlled by observed root variables.
The gID algorithm is sound and complete under positivity of the observational distribution.
Possible-world diagrams give a complete solution to possibilistic causal compatibility.
Finite latent cardinality bounds can preserve multiple independent sources.
Canonical finite response types reduce discrete causal bounds to polynomial programs.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Only the Shpitser--Pearl comparison has a proved conditional containment relation.  The Chen--Darwiche comparisons are theorem-specific premise separations or informed-by relations and do not establish global class containment.

prose_updates.tldr: This note formulates, but does not construct, a bounded support-aware grammar for FID-S. The intended procedure concerns finite latent DAGs with supplied observed alphabets, qualitative functional nodes, and declared positive or zero observed events, and would return an inconsistency certificate, a guarded identifying formula, or an exact-support rational separating pair. The proved classical result is conditional and abstract: any restricted grammar instance satisfying the local seven-case interface reproduces ordinary ID; no such concrete FID-S grammar instance is constructed here. The fully observed completion frontier is proved: for each obstruction and each integer \(r\geq 3\), an existentially selected common-law fiber has target gap at least \(1-2/r\), primitive denominator at most \(r|V|\max_{i\in V}|\Omega_i|\), and the stated logarithmic primitive-bit bound. The case \(r=8\) gives the \(3/4\)-gap corollary, but no constant-gap claim is made for every fixed observational law on the same support. The supported-bow pattern is resolved directly by its proposition, thereby furnishing a mandatory regression instance for any future support trichotomy. The general support-preserving independent-source latent lift, rational equal-law witness theorem, converse formula reconstruction, concrete finite grammar, certificate syntax, and global search bounds remain open.

project_justification.fill: If the latent-lifting OEQ is resolved, the resulting FID-S procedure will preserve \(\Omega\), exact support, functional-row provenance, and the latent-source architecture and will return the stated three certificate types. What is proved now is only the universal conditional compiler theorem for an abstract instance satisfying the local classical-ID interface. Separately, the fully observed frontier has a parameterized rational smoothing certificate: for every integer \(r\geq3\), each completion obstruction admits an existentially chosen same-law exact-support pair with gap at least \(1-2/r\) and primitive bit cost growing as \(O(\log r)\); this does not construct or settle the latent grammar.

prose_updates.related_work: Shpitser and Pearl supply the recursive seven-case ID algorithm, its soundness and completeness results, and the hedge results with their proper failed-subquery and existential original-query scopes. The only containment established in this note is the conditional full-support, \(W=\varnothing\) embedding of classical ID: every abstract restricted grammar satisfying the local seven-case interface has the same call tree and normalized successful expression, but no concrete FID-S instance of that interface is constructed. The comparison papers do not supply the complete exact-support rational-countermodel trichotomy requested by the latent-lifting OEQ, and this note does not yet supply it either. Chen--Darwiche's functional-elimination, treatment-positivity, constrained-identifiability, and strictly positive state-based results are used only for theorem-specific premise separations or informed-by comparisons; they do not establish a global inclusion between their regimes and the arbitrary support-literal regime here. The same is true of the cited context-specific, generalized-identification, possibilistic-compatibility, latent-cardinality, and response-coordinate results: they provide non-subsumption facts, uncovered residual regimes, or ingredients, not global class inclusions. The supported-bow pattern is resolved directly by the dedicated proposition, thereby furnishing a mandatory regression instance for any future support trichotomy. The support-preserving independent-source rational lift remains explicitly open.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The following are proved: the finite support oracle; the fully observed completion frontier and guarded identifying formula; for every integer \(r\geq3\), the fully observed existential-fiber smoothing certificate with gap at least \(1-2/r\), denominator bound \(r|V|\max_{i\in V}|\Omega_i|\), and logarithmic primitive-bit cost; the supported-bow formula and exact rational separating pair; and the universally quantified conditional classical-ID compiler theorem for every abstract grammar instance satisfying the local seven-case interface. The following are not constructed or proved: a concrete FID-S grammar or compiler satisfying that interface; the general support-preserving independent-source latent lift; a general rational equal-law witness theorem; converse guarded-formula reconstruction in the latent case; terminal-certificate syntax; the kill-instance audit against concrete productions; and explicit global search, latent-cardinality, and certificate-bit bounds. The parameterized constant gap is existentially obtained by choosing a fully observed observational fiber for each completion obstruction and is not asserted for every fixed law with that support. A failure pair is scoped to its actual failed query or subquery, and only the published existential-subquery hedge conclusion is carried back to the original query. Generic real quantifier elimination, unrestricted latent flattening, and the fully observed special case do not resolve the latent headline.
